items.rationale: Reviewed 2026-10-18: def:return-measures describes holding-period, price and total, cumulative, arithmetic and geometric, annualised, log, gross and net, real, leveraged, time- and money-weighted returns, compares them and states which question each answers.

items.paraphrase: Interpret required returns, risk-free rates, risk premia and inflation
items.rationale: Reviewed 2026-10-18: def:required-return-components defines the risk-free rate, real rate and expected inflation (Fisher, exact and approximate), and the inflation-risk, term, liquidity, credit and equity premia, interpreting each and how they combine.

items.paraphrase: Calculate and compare return types for assets, instruments and indicators
items.rationale: Reviewed 2026-10-18: def:return-measures calculates and compares returns for a share (price, income, total), an index (price against total return), a portfolio (time- and money-weighted, gross and net of fees) and series (arithmetic, geometric, annualised, log, real, leveraged).

items.paraphrase: Calculate and compare money- and time-weighted returns
items.rationale: Reviewed: def:return-measures calculates both returns on one cash-flow history, compares them on matching horizons and explains the difference and the choice; the bullet asks no more.

items.paraphrase: Index weighting choices; calculate index value and return
items.rationale: Reviewed 2026-10-18 against the outline page: meth:index-value-return-calculation describes price, capitalisation (float-adjusted), equal and capped weighting with their implications (price-level dependence, rebalancing turnover), and calculates and interprets index levels and price, total and net total returns with divisor adjustments for a split and a share issue.

items.paraphrase: Present value of fixed-income and equity cash flows
items.rationale: Reviewed 2026-10-18: meth:instrument-present-value calculates and interprets present values of a zero-coupon bond, a coupon bond at one yield and at zero rates, a preferred share, and common shares under constant and two-stage dividend growth.

items.paraphrase: Implied return and implied growth from price and cash flows
items.rationale: Reviewed 2026-10-18: meth:instrument-present-value solves a bond yield from price, the required return implied by price and growth, and the growth implied by price and required return, and interprets them as model-implied, not forecasts.

items.paraphrase: Cash-flow additivity, no arbitrage, implied forwards and option values
items.rationale: Reviewed 2026-10-18: res:cash-flow-additivity explains additivity and no arbitrage and applies them to an implied forward rate, a forward exchange rate and a replicated one-period option with put-call parity.

items.paraphrase: Central tendency, location and dispersion measures
items.rationale: Reviewed 2026-10-18: def:return-sample-statistics calculates mean, median, mode, range, absolute deviations, variance and standard deviation with both denominators and percentiles under a stated rule, interprets them on a return sample and evaluates which measure suits tails and skew.

Reviewed 2026-10-18: def:return-shape-statistics defines and computes skewness and kurtosis, separates raw and excess kurtosis and the bias-adjusted versions, interprets their signs and evaluates their reliability in short samples.
Reviewed 2026-10-18: def:return-dependence calculates covariance and correlation with stated denominators and units, interprets them and evaluates their limits (linearity, outliers, instability).

Reviewed 2026-10-18: def:downside-relative-dispersion calculates semi-deviation for stated targets and denominators and the coefficient of variation, interprets them and evaluates the CV's failure when the mean is near zero or negative.

items.paraphrase: Unconditional expected mean, variance and covariance
items.rationale: Reviewed 2026-10-18: def:conditional-moments calculates unconditional expected values, variances and covariance from a probability table and interprets them as model moments distinct from sample statistics.

items.paraphrase: Moments of key distributions used in finance
items.rationale: Reviewed 2026-10-18: def:financial-distributions calculates and interprets the moments of the normal, lognormal, Student t, binomial and uniform distributions, states when moments exist and evaluates the fit of each to financial variables. The outline does not name the distributions; chi-square and F, used in inference, are treated in meth:hypothesis-testing (2026-10-18).
Reviewed 2026-10-18: def:conditional-moments calculates conditional expectations, variances and covariances by state and verifies the laws of total expectation, variance and covariance.
Reviewed 2026-10-18: meth:bayesian-updating formulates an investment question as a discrete prior updated by a likelihood, with explicit normalisation, posterior and predictive probability.

items.paraphrase: Central limit theorem, confidence intervals and sampling
items.rationale: Reviewed 2026-10-18: meth:confidence-intervals explains the central limit theorem with its assumptions, sampling methods and sampling bias, and the construction and repeated-sampling meaning of t, normal and chi-square confidence intervals, including their failure under dependence.

items.paraphrase: Hypothesis testing: significance, error types, power, construction
items.rationale: Reviewed 2026-10-18: meth:hypothesis-testing explains hypotheses, significance, p-values, Type I and II errors and power, constructs t, chi-square and F tests on the example and interprets the decisions; re-reviewed 2026-10-18 after the F-test correction: the variance-ratio example now satisfies and states the independent-samples condition.

Reviewed 2026-10-18: meth:nonparametric-tests compares the t, signed-rank and sign tests, states when each is appropriate and their assumptions and power, constructs all three on one sample and interprets the results.

items.paraphrase: Portfolio expected return, variance, covariance and correlation
items.rationale: Reviewed 2026-10-18 against the outline wording (PDF and printed p. 2: calculate, interpret and evaluate the expected return, variance, standard deviation, covariance and correlation of portfolio returns) and meth:portfolio-return-moments: one-period value-weighted portfolio return, expected return, variance and standard deviation in expanded and matrix form, covariance and correlation between two portfolios (P and Q), with model moments and historical estimates computed and interpreted on worked examples; evaluation by comparison with the weighted average and the component moments. The item's minimum-variance and optimal-portfolio neighbours (b02, b03) are separate items, not part of this one.

Reviewed 2026-10-18 against the outline page and the finished entries: meth:efficient-frontier describes the minimum-variance frontier and the global minimum-variance portfolio, calculates them (closed forms under a budget constraint with their conditions, and a three-fund table checked by optimiser) and interprets efficient against dominated portfolios, long-only boundary solutions and infeasible targets.

items.paraphrase: Optimal portfolio from risk aversion, CAL and CML
items.rationale: Reviewed 2026-10-18 against the outline page and the finished entries: meth:capital-allocation-line explains choosing the point on the CAL from risk aversion (y* with a worked table and figure, def:risk-aversion-utility for the utility) and its extension to the market portfolio and the CML under the equilibrium assumptions of Sharpe and Fama-French.

Reviewed 2026-10-18 and re-reviewed after the correction of the same day: meth:historical-simulation describes the method and explains its use for VaR and ES on an example, with equal and age weights under one (lower-quantile, exact-tail-mass) convention, Hull's rank convention attributed as an alternative, and the method's assumptions.
Reviewed 2026-10-18: meth:bootstrap-resampling describes the bootstrap and explains its use for a standard error and interval, its sampling unit and its failure for dependent returns.

items.paraphrase: Monte Carlo simulation and its uses
items.rationale: Reviewed 2026-10-18: meth:monte-carlo-simulation describes Monte Carlo simulation and explains its use for an option value and a probability, with seed, standard error and an analytic benchmark.

Reviewed 2026-10-18 against the outline wording (describe, interpret and explain simple linear regression, including coefficient estimation by the least squares criterion) and meth:simple-regression-estimation: population line, least squares criterion and formulas, fitted values and residuals, coefficient units and interpretation, association against causation, on a worked example. Re-reviewed 2026-10-18 after the correction pass (plan sec. 13.5) against the same outline wording: the entry now also states when the estimates exist and are unique (finite data, Sxx > 0) and that fitting needs no error assumption; still covered.

items.paraphrase: Assumptions, residual diagnostics, fit and ANOVA
items.rationale: Reviewed 2026-10-18 against the outline wording (describe and compare the assumptions, identify violations through residuals, evaluate goodness of fit, coefficients and ANOVA results) and meth:regression-diagnostics-anova: the four conditions and the sensitivity of tests and intervals to each, residual plots and standardised residuals, S, R^2 and its cautions, coefficient t tests and intervals, the ANOVA table and F = t^2 for the zero-slope null, on a worked example with a counterexample. Re-reviewed 2026-10-18 after the correction pass (plan sec. 13.5): the comparison of assumptions now separates computing, unbiasedness, conventional variances and exact t/F inference, requires n > 2, and restricts F = t^2 to the matching null; still covered.

items.paraphrase: Predictions, standard error of estimate, prediction intervals, functional forms
items.rationale: Reviewed 2026-10-18 against the outline wording (calculate and interpret predicted values, the standard error of the estimate and prediction intervals; describe functional forms) and meth:regression-prediction-functional-form: predictions, standard error of estimate, fit and prediction, the interval for the mean against the prediction interval, extrapolation, level-level, log-level, level-log and log-log forms with units and domains, and retransformation to geometric means, medians and means. Re-reviewed 2026-10-18 after the correction pass (plan sec. 13.5): the log-log percentage rule is now 100 (1.01^b1 - 1), and the back-transformed log prediction is the geometric mean, the median only under a median-zero log error; still covered.

Reviewed 2026-10-18 against the outline page and the finished entries: meth:capm-regression calculates alpha, beta, standard errors, intervals and R^2 from a declared twelve-month sample by closed forms and two least-squares routes, and interprets units, fit, uncertainty, raw against excess returns and why alpha is not skill.
